classification.difficultyReason: Complete a supplied sine graph using its stated odd symmetry.

content.prompt:
$y=\sin\theta$ is an odd function as $\sin(-\theta)=-\sin\theta$.
Complete the graph for the domain $-360^{\circ}\leq\theta\leq360^{\circ}$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6 graph at the bottom of the page
spec.description: Square coordinate grid with 45-degree horizontal steps and one-third vertical steps. Both axes have two arrowheads. The negative-angle half is blank; the supplied sine curve occupies 0 to 360 degrees. The source origin O is omitted under house graph conventions.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal coordinate u represents theta=45u degrees. Grid extends from -450 to 450 degrees and from -4/3 to 4/3. Supplied curve is y=sin(theta), 0<=theta<=360 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the positive-angle curve is supplied in the question.

answer.short: Complete the negative-angle half through $(-360^{\circ},0)$, $(-270^{\circ},1)$, $(-180^{\circ},0)$, $(-90^{\circ},-1)$ and $(0^{\circ},0)$ with a smooth sine curve.
answer.worked: Since $\sin(-\theta)=-\sin\theta$, rotate the supplied curve through $180^{\circ}$ about the origin. The missing curve passes through $(-360^{\circ},0)$, $(-270^{\circ},1)$, $(-180^{\circ},0)$, $(-90^{\circ},-1)$ and $(0^{\circ},0)$.

spec.description: Complete self-contained sine graph on the same coordinate frame as the question, including the required negative-angle curve.
spec.mathematics: y=sin(theta) for -360<=theta<=360 degrees; odd symmetry about the origin.
spec.answerVisibility: Completed graph appears only in answer editions.
